title: Build a Windowed Stream Aggregator with Watermarks
summary:
Build the core of Flink, Kafka Streams and Beam: **event-time** windowed aggregation per key. You implement **tumbling** and **sliding (hopping)** window assignment, a **watermark** (`max event time − allowed out-of-orderness`), firing on watermark, and **allowed lateness** that re-emits updated results with increasing revisions. Events that are too late are **dropped or sent to a side output**. On the sink side, an **idempotent upsert table** makes re-emission and replays safe.

This is the vocabulary of every "design a real-time analytics / metrics / billing pipeline" interview: *what is a watermark, what happens to late data, how do you avoid double counting with an at-least-once source?* The final test checks your streaming results against a batch computation on a shuffled stream of 3,000 events.

milestones.name: M1: Window assignment and aggregators
milestones.description: Epoch-aligned, half-open tumbling and sliding windows, including negatives and gaps; `sum`, `count`, `max` and `avg` aggregators.

milestones.name: M2: Watermarks and firing
milestones.description: Watermark = max event time − out-of-orderness, monotonic. A window fires once the watermark passes its end. Out-of-order events within the bound land in their event-time window.

milestones.name: M3: Late data
milestones.description: Events behind every one of their windows are dropped and counted, or sent to a side output. A partly-late sliding event still feeds its open windows.

milestones.name: M4: Allowed lateness and idempotent sinks
milestones.description: Late updates re-emit with revision + 1; state is purged after `end + allowedLateness`; a `ResultTable` upsert sink ignores stale and duplicate revisions.

milestones.name: M5: Exactly-once-ish results
milestones.description: Dedupe by event id, explicit watermarks for idle sources, `flush`, deterministic firing order, and equality with a batch computation on a shuffled stream.
